text:
Ding 

 
 Toasts with real spring physics. 
 One toast that morphs in place. No dependencies. React, Svelte, Vue or plain DOM.
 

 
 Home ·
 Docs ·
 npm 
 

 
 
 

---

 Why Ding

- Morphs by default. New calls reuse a quick toast; errors and other held toasts keep their place unless you choose held: 'replace' .
- Real springs. Size, shape and text move on a spring solver, so interrupting an animation keeps its momentum.
- No stylesheet. Styles are injected from JavaScript. Nothing to import.
- Light, dark and system themes , six positions, right-to-left support.
- Easy to restyle. Colors and corner radius are CSS variables.
- Rich content. Description, avatar, buttons, progress bar, a countdown line, small trailing text.
- Accessible by default. Persistent live regions, keyboard dismiss, prefers-reduced-motion .
- Optional sound. A soft built-in tone per status, or plug in your own.
- Strict TypeScript , ESM and CommonJS builds.

 Install

 

Each framework package depends on the small @yusufceng1z/ding core, so you install only one.

Using shadcn/ui? Ding is in the shadcn registry directory, so one command installs the React package and adds a ding-toaster.tsx wrapper:

 

 Optional Ding skill

The Ding skill gives Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and other Agent Skills-compatible tools framework setup and guidance on promises, progress, and toast actions.

Run the installer from your app with Node.js 22.20 or newer, then select your coding agent.

 

Add --global to use the skill across projects. For manual installation, copy the ding skill directory into your agent's project skills directory. In Claude Code, that directory is .claude/skills/ and the command is /ding .

For Claude chat, create an uploadable ZIP from a clone of the Ding repository.

 

Upload ding-skill.zip under Customize → Skills . Claude's upload guide

 Quick start

Render the toaster once, then call toast from anywhere.

Guides for React, Svelte, Vue and Nuxt, and plain JavaScript.

 React 

 

Works in the Next.js App Router as is: the package ships "use client" , so Toaster can go straight into app/layout.tsx . Call toast.configure from a client component, in an effect. See the Next.js guide.

 Svelte 5 

 

 Vue 3 

 

 Toaster renders nothing in place and mounts in onMounted , so server rendering is safe. In Nuxt, put it in app.vue and call toast from client code.

 Plain DOM 

 

 Usage

 

Toast show calls return a caller ID; toast.promise() returns the supplied promise.

 Promises and updates

 

Only the newest caller can update the shared toast, so a slow request that finishes late cannot overwrite a newer message.

 Actions

A synchronous onClick may return a patch to morph the toast in place. An async action closes on click; show its outcome as a separate toast, or use toast.promise() for a loading-to-result morph.

 

 Options

 Option Description 
 --- --- 
 description Second line of text 
 action { label, onClick } , the main button 
 secondary { label, onClick } , a quieter button beside the action 
 image Avatar or thumbnail URL, replaces the status icon 
 meta Small trailing text, such as now or ⌘V 
 progress 0 to 1 , draws a thin bar at the bottom 
 duration Milliseconds before it closes. 0 keeps it until dismissed. Default 5000 
 id Reuse an id so repeated calls from one place stay one caller 

By default, errors, loading toasts and toasts with a button stay until dismissed. Hover, keyboard focus and a hidden tab pause the countdown on timed toasts. Repeating the same toast adds a counter (×2).

 Configure

 

 dismiss(id) uses the id returned by a toast call. If a newer call takes over that toast, dismissing the old id does nothing. Custom renderers should use toast.close(item.id) to close the visible toast by its ToastItem.id ; this also works after a takeover.

 Held toasts

A toast is held when it stays until dismissed: an error, a toast with a button, or one with duration: 0 . A loading toast is not held, because it is about to turn into its result. held decides what happens when another toast arrives while a held toast is on screen:

 Value Behavior 
 --- --- 
 'list' (default) The held toast keeps its place. Quick toasts appear next to it, and a new held toast takes over the quick one. 
 'queue' New toasts wait in order and show one after another once the held toast is gone. 
 'replace' A new toast morphs the one on screen, held or not. This is how 0.0.5 behaved. 

 

Set it with toast.configure , or pass held to mountToaster in plain DOM.

 Styling

Colors and corner radius are CSS variables. Set them in your own stylesheet and they apply to every toast, in any framework:

 

 Variable Default Controls 
 --- --- --- 
 --tst-radius 22px Corner radius. The default makes a pill 
 --tst-bg light-dark( fff, 0c0c0d) Background 
 --tst-fg light-dark( 0f0f13, fafafa) Text 
 --tst-success light-dark( 12a36b, 4ade80) Success icon 
 --tst-error light-dark( e5484d, f87171) Error icon 
 --tst-warning light-dark( c77d00, fbbf24) Warning icon 
 --tst-info light-dark( 2f7de1, 60a5fa) Info icon 

The defaults follow the theme through light-dark() . A single value applies to both themes. To keep them apart, write your own: --tst-bg: light-dark( fff, 111) .

 Advanced styling

More hooks, for when colors and radius are not enough:

 Variable Default Controls 
 --- --- --- 
 --tst-size 44px Height of the pill, and the width of the icon circle 
 --tst-pad 16px Distance from the screen edge 
 --tst-shadow built in Shadow around the toast 
 --tst-enter-scale built in How small the toast starts when it arrives 

The font comes from .tst-viewport , so set font-family and font-size there.

 Filled toasts. Each toast exposes --fill (surface), --on (text, buttons, close button, focus ring) and --c (icon color) per status. Override them to fill the whole toast with its status color:

 

 Light and dark. Ding follows the system by default. If your site has its own theme switch, such as a .dark class, pass

install.title: Install
install.html:
npm i @yusufceng1z/ding-react    # React 18+
npm i @yusufceng1z/ding-svelte   # Svelte 5
npm i @yusufceng1z/ding-vue      # Vue 3 and Nuxt
npm i @yusufceng1z/ding          # plain DOM

Each framework package depends on the small @yusufceng1z/ding core, so you install only one.

Using shadcn/ui? Ding is in the shadcn registry directory, so one command installs the React package and adds a ding-toaster.tsx wrapper:

npx shadcn@latest add @ding/ding
Optional Ding skill

The Ding skill gives Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and other Agent Skills-compatible tools framework setup and guidance on promises, progress, and toast actions.

Run the installer from your app with Node.js 22.20 or newer, then select your coding agent.

npx skills add YusufCeng1z/ding --skill ding

Add --global to use the skill across projects. For manual installation, copy the ding skill directory into your agent's project skills directory. In Claude Code, that directory is .claude/skills/ and the command is /ding.

For Claude chat, create an uploadable ZIP from a clone of the Ding repository.

git archive --format=zip --output=ding-skill.zip HEAD:.agents/skills ding

Upload ding-skill.zip under Customize → Skills. Claude's upload guide

usage.title: Usage
usage.html:
toast.success('Saved');
toast.error('Payment failed', { description: 'Card declined' });
toast.warning('Storage almost full');
toast.info('New version available');
toast.loading('Uploading…');

Toast show calls return a caller ID; toast.promise() returns the supplied promise.

Promises and updates
toast.promise(save(), {
  loading: 'Saving…',
  success: 'Saved',
  error: (err) => `Could not save: ${err.message}`,
});

const id = toast.loading('Uploading photo…', { progress: 0 });
toast.update(id, { progress: 0.6 });
toast.update(id, { type: 'success', title: 'Photo uploaded', progress: null });

Only the newest caller can update the shared toast, so a slow request that finishes late cannot overwrite a newer message.

Actions

A synchronous onClick may return a patch to morph the toast in place. An async action closes on click; show its outcome as a separate toast, or use toast.promise() for a loading-to-result morph.

toast.success('Message deleted', {
  action: {
    label: 'Undo',
    onClick: () => {
      restore();
      return { type: 'info', title: 'Restored' };
    },
  },
});
